summary: registry/ui/motion.browser.test.tsx — the assertion ADR 0018 named as the highest-leverage motion item left, and the first thing in this repo that can tell a working transition from a dead one. Every other layer only sees the declaration: check:motion reads source, check:utilities resolves the class, and a visual baseline is a single frame in which nothing is moving. That gap has shipped real defects twice — Modal and Popover both wrote `transition-[opacity,transform]` beside `scale-98`, which in Tailwind v4 covers nothing, and a Popover test asserting transitionProperty contained 'transform' passed for the defect's entire life because the declaration reads back identically whether or not anything animates. Ten assertions, all through getAnimations(): that each duration token resolves to a real number in the emitted stylesheet; that Switch's thumb and Tabs' trigger run at --ui-duration-fast; that Accordion's panel animates HEIGHT and Progress' fill animates WIDTH, both at --ui-duration-base, with the property asserted as well as the timing; and that Skeleton's and Button's keyframes loop, Skeleton's at --ui-duration-loop. Shared rather than per-component on purpose: what is being checked is the system property that nothing animates at a number the token layer does not know about, and a per-component version of that is 29 chances to forget. Two things learned while writing it, both recorded in the file: a synthetic .click() returns before the browser has recalculated style, so getAnimations() is empty on WORKING code and the assertions must be driven by real Playwright clicks; and a transition needs a previously-computed value to start from, so Progress' width must be read once before it is changed or the element takes 80% as its first computed value and never transitions. Both produce a green-looking failure, which is the category this file exists for. All four probes — wrong token, wrong property, off-token keyframe, un-animated height — were confirmed to fail it.
